The Learning Deck / Year 8

Between the lines.

Spot the clue. Make the connection.

First-try points0 / 12
Explicit = saidThe text tells you directly.
Implicit = hintedThe writer suggests an idea.
Infer = work it outThe reader uses the clues.
Writers imply. Readers infer. Same idea, different sides.Warm-up · No timer. Think it through.

The tiny field guide

Explicit: “Ben was frightened.” The writer tells us directly.

Implicit: “At every creak, Ben spun round.” The writer hints at fear without naming it.

Inference: “I think Ben is frightened because he reacts to every noise.” The reader works it out.

These are not three separate boxes. Ben’s fear is implicit in the text. We infer that fear from the clues.

A useful sentence:
I infer that ___ because the text says “___”, which suggests ___.

For the teacher · How to play
  • Allow about 15–20 minutes. Play together on the board or individually. Students can vote A, B or C before you tap.
  • Start with the three warm-up buttons. Ask: “Who leaves the hint? Who works it out?”
  • There are 12 questions. First-try answers earn a point; mistakes give feedback and another attempt. No points are lost.
  • Ask for evidence from the words. The illustrations support atmosphere but are not additional textual evidence.
  • “Probably” and “may” are useful: an inference can be well supported without being certain. Other interpretations can work if students justify them.
  • The final writing task uses a model and self-check. It is not automatically graded.
  • This file works offline. Progress and writing last until the page is reloaded.
